title: Fewshot Patchwork — studio experiments
body:
Purpose:
- Working notes for a small lab to try "patchwork" few-shot sets: assemble few-shots at inference time from multiple micro-exemplars instead of a single contiguous examples block. Goal: improve robustness to task framing drift and shorter token budgets.

Hypotheses:
1) A patchwork of 3–5 micro-exemplars (each 8–30 tokens) that are topically diverse but structurally aligned reduces hallucination on slot-filling tasks.
2) Dynamically selecting exemplars by surface-level similarity + structural signal outperforms naive nearest-neighbor by 4–6% accuracy on our synthetic suite.
3) Interleaving a 1-line instruction between exemplars (separator prompt) reduces model tendency to merge outputs across exemplars.

Quick experimental plan (mini A/B):
- Model: open-vicuna-13b-quant (hosted dev region) and local quant7 runner.
- Metric: slot-level precision/recall, hallucination rate (tokens not in any exemplar or instruction), span-boundary errors.
- Configs: static-block baseline (3 full examples), patchwork-static (3 micro-exemplars handpicked), patchwork-dynamic (kNN+struct filter), patchwork-dynamic+separator.
- Shots: 3 total micro-exemplars per prompt; budget ≤ 120 tokens for context.

Micro-exemplar bank (sketch):
- EX1: "Q: What's the price of the Pro widget?
A: $199.99 (USD)"
- EX2: "Q: Delivery ETA for order #B21?
A: 3 business days"
- EX3: "Q: Can I mix colors on a single order?
A: Yes — select variants at checkout"
- EX4: "Q: Refund window length?
A: 30 days from delivery"
- EX5: "Q: Is international shipping available?
A: Yes, shipping zones apply"
- EX6: "Q: How to apply discount codes?
A: Enter at cart, one code per order"

Prompts (draft templates):
- TEMPLATE A (static-block):
  Instruction: "Extract a single concise answer to the question from the examples."
  Examples: EX1
            EX2
  Query: "Q: Will I be charged import duties for an order to NL?"

- TEMPLATE B (patchwork-dynamic):
  Instruction: "Use the short exemplars below as patterns. Answer concisely; mention currencies only if present in examples."
  Micro-exemplars: [select 3 by similarity to query + structural diversity filter]
  Separator: "---"
  Query: "Q: How long until my order ships?"

Observed failures during quick runs (notes):
- Failure mode: exemplar bleed — model copies phrasing from an earlier exemplar's answer and applies it to a different question (e.g., uses $199.99 when answer should be ETA). Occurs when exemplars contain overlapping lexical anchors (dates, prices).
- Failure mode: overgeneralization from negative exemplars — if one exemplar states "no" for a variant, model sometimes assumes "no" for similar but different variant.
- Failure mode: instruction overshadowing — when instruction mentions "concise" and examples are verbose, model produces terse but incomplete answers.

Small diagnostic cases (to reproduce):
1) Query: "Q: What's the warranty period for the Pro widget?"
   Bank: EX1, EX4, EX6
   Expected: "1 year" or "12 months" (we don't have explicit example; check model hallucination frequency)
   Observed: model often replies with price or refund window (hallucination).

2) Query: "Q: Can I add a gift message to my order?"
   Bank: EX3, EX6, EX5
   Observed: sometimes model answers about mixing colors, not gift messages — structural mismatch.

Heuristics to try next (prioritized):
- Structural tagging for each micro-exemplar: label as [policy],[logistics],[payment],[variant]. Prefer at least 2 different labels per patchwork to avoid topical collapse.
- Penalize repeat entity types across selected exemplars (if two examples both have currency tokens, deprioritize one).
- Add a one-sentence "format hint" after each exemplar: "Answer uses short phrases" to align length (cheap nudge).
- Alternate separator token between exemplars ("---","***") to test whether surface separators reduce bleed.

Mini test harness ideas:
- Offline scorer: levenshtein overlap + entity-level checks to categorize hallucination types.
- Randomized seeds: run 10 seed variations per prompt set to measure variance.
- Embed-based candidate pool: use a tiny bi-encoder to compute top-12, then apply structural filter to pick 3.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Build small UI in console where I can drag exemplar cards into slots — helps subjective sanity checks.
- Create a small CSV of ~150 queries across logistics/payment/returns/variants for consistent benchmarking.
- Add one more failure logging field in the harness: "bleed_source": which exemplar likely caused the wrong entity.
- Check with SRE about request concurrency limits on dev hosted region (we're running many short queries).

Random observations and micro-experiments (raw):
- When I switched separator from newline to "***" the model seemed slightly less likely to copy numeric tokens across exemplars (n=40, anecdotal).
- Putting a short negative exemplar ("Q: Do you ship to Antarctica? A: No") reduces false-positives for exotic regions when included, but increases conservatism elsewhere. Tradeoff.

Example few-shot set I want to try next (compact):
Instruction: "Answer with a single sentence. If unknown, say 'I don't know; check support.'"
Micro-exs: EX2, EX4, EX6
Query batch: ["Is international shipping available to DE?","What's the refund window for digital goods?","How to apply discount codes?"]
Expected: concise, correct or safe fallback.

Meta questions for follow-up:
- Is patchwork more robust across prompt format drift than contiguous few-shots when we add user-provided context (e.g., order numbers)?
- Does separator type interact with tokenization boundaries for the model family we use?

End-of-note quick checklist:
- [ ] Implement structural tags and selection filter (by 2025-03-09)
- [ ] Prepare the 150-query CSV (by 2025-03-16)
- [ ] Wire in small harness to log bleed_source (by 2025-03-20)
- [ ] Run full comparatives across 2 models (hosted + local) (by 2025-04-01)

Scratch: sample interaction dump (raw):
Prompt used:
"Instruction: Use the examples below as a pattern. Answer concisely.
***
Q: What's the price of the Pro widget?
A: $199.99 (USD)
***
Q: Delivery ETA for order #B21?
A: 3 business days
***
Q: How to apply discount codes?
A: Enter at cart, one code per order
***
Q: Can I mix colors on a single order?
A:"
Model reply (bad): "$199.99 — you can mix colors at checkout"
Notes: we want to force a single concise answer ("Yes — select variants at checkout") but model prefixed price. Need stronger structural cues or entity masking.

End.
